rows.result: Probability measures provide the unrestricted mixing-law domain and the minimum predicate states the negative-log-likelihood optimum.
rows.gap: The Gaussian-convolution objective and global minimizer existence must be supplied; no uniqueness or fixed-grid restriction is part of the definition.

comparisons.D3: For the fixed N>0 observations minimize ell_N(rho)=-(1/N)*sum_i log(integral phi(X_i-y) drho(y)) over ALL Borel probability measures on R^d. The positive bounded Gaussian kernel ensures each mixture density at a fixed observation is finite and strictly positive, so the log is used on its intended domain. Do not restrict to measures with a prescribed number of atoms, a preselected grid, an absolutely continuous density or a finite-second-moment subclass. IsMinOn over bundled ProbabilityMeasure states the optimization property but does not establish attainment or choose a measurable estimator. The registered source explicitly uses NPMLE for any minimizer when uniqueness is not supplied; its theorem’s existence claim remains separate from the definition.

rows.result: Mathlib’s topological measure support is closed, conull in Euclidean space and contained in every closed conull set.
rows.gap: The existing measure-support definition agrees with the paper’s smallest closed full-mass set for Borel probabilities on R^d.

comparisons.D5: Use the topological support of rho on real Euclidean space. Its every-neighborhood-positive-mass characterization makes it closed; the inspected support_mem_ae result applies in the hereditarily Lindelof Euclidean space, giving mass one for a probability law. The inspected support_subset_of_isClosed property gives minimality among closed full-mass sets. This is not the nonzero set of a chosen density representative or just the finite set of atoms with positive singleton mass. A full-support law has positive mass in every nonempty open ball, whereas a finite atomic initialization cannot have support all R^d in positive dimension.

rows.result: The library theorem characterizes convergence of probability measures by integrals of every bounded continuous real function.
rows.gap: The theorem directly matches the source weak-convergence definition after bundling the measures and using the sequence filter at infinity.

comparisons.D7: Bundle each rho_n and rho as a ProbabilityMeasure on Euclidean R^d with its Borel sigma-algebra and use Tendsto atTop to the neighborhood filter of rho. The theorem quantifies all bounded continuous real functions via the bundled BoundedContinuousFunction type, equivalent to the source’s unbundled bounded-and-continuous test functions. Indices start at n=0, which does not affect the filter formulation. This is weak convergence, not density-pointwise, total-variation or W2 convergence, and it does not assert convergence of unbounded second moments. The paper’s optimization results assume such a limit exists; this characterization does not prove existence of a limit.

rows.result: A constrained minimum and signed-measure differences can express components of the formal metric-gradient construction.
rows.gap: The topology, positive-step limit, admissible curve and optimizer selection must be specified; the source expressly omits existence of the limiting curve.

comparisons.D15: At fixed rho_t minimize the LINEARIZED first-variation objective integral delta_ell_N(rho_t) d(rho-rho_t) plus d(rho,rho_t)^2/(2*eta) over probability rho. This is not the full nonlinear proximal objective ell_N(rho)+distance penalty. Express the signed integral as a difference of two integrals with their integrability conditions, or embed finite laws in SignedMeasure; ordinary Measure subtraction is not signed subtraction. The overview prints eta→0 without a topology for the difference quotient, a positive-side restriction or a choice among minimizers. A generic Tendsto predicate cannot determine those choices or identify them with weak, total-variation or distributional convergence. Preserve the stated omission of existence of an absolutely continuous limiting curve instead of selecting a library topology and declaring the gradient flow constructed.

rows.result: Reweighting by the displayed nonnegative multiplier expresses the Fisher-Rao Euler update and its intended RN derivative.
rows.gap: Nonnegativity of the multiplier and its unit integral must be justified for the actual step size, preserving the source gamma/eta mismatch in the later theorem.

comparisons.D13: Set w_n(x)=1-gamma*(1+delta_ell_N(rho_n)(x)) and rho_(n+1)=rho_n.withDensity(w_n) only after proving w_n>=0 almost everywhere and using its finite nonnegative conversion. The explicit first variation has integral -1 under rho_n, which yields integral w_n=1, but normalization alone does not imply nonnegativity. The definition says gamma>0 without a sufficient upper bound; 0<gamma<=1 is one immediate sufficient range from delta_ell_N<=0, not a quoted restriction to insert into the source. The RN identity is rho_n-almost everywhere and implies absolute continuity, so a fixed-support iteration cannot create mass outside the previous support. Do not use ENNReal.ofReal to clip negative multipliers, because that changes the update. Theorem4 names eta rather than gamma; retain that separate notation issue instead of silently identifying them.

rows.result: A density reweighting followed by a pushforward gives the two ordered splitting steps.
rows.gap: The nonnegative unit-mass intermediate law and measurable transport map must be justified, with the gradient evaluated at the intermediate measure.

comparisons.D10: First form rho_tilde_n from rho_n with multiplier 1-eta*(1+delta_ell_N(rho_n)); then transport that INTERMEDIATE law by x↦x-eta*gradient(delta_ell_N(rho_tilde_n))(x). Do not evaluate the second gradient at rho_n or reverse the two updates. The source’s explicit first-variation normalization is essential for mass preservation; adding an arbitrary constant to it changes the reaction step. The positive eta statement alone does not ensure nonnegative weights, and a totalized withDensity conversion must not clip negative values. Once rho_tilde_n is a probability and the map is measurable, pushforward preserves mass; generic gradient needs the intended differentiability. The finite-particle Algorithm1 has a different printed location-before-weight order and indexing issues and must not be substituted for (3.7). The convergence theorem assumes full support and weak convergence rather than guaranteeing either for arbitrary particles.

rows.result: Centered reaction rates and their squared integrated action can be written using scalar test-function derivatives and nonnegative time-space integration.
rows.gap: The admissible probability curves, endpoint and analytic conditions must be supplied, and the separate Hellinger formula is not certified equivalent to this centered action.

comparisons.D16: Use curves rho_t joining the specified rho0,rho1 over t in[0,1] and reaction rate alpha_t-integral alpha_t drho_t. The source’s distributional convention means for each smooth compactly supported phi the derivative of integral phi drho_t equals integral phi*(alpha_t-mean_rho_t(alpha_t)) drho_t. Centering makes total reaction mass zero when the relevant integrations and time differentiation are justified. Minimize the integrated SQUARE of the centered rate over admissible curves; this is the displayed squared distance/action, not a square root of the integrand. The prose supplies endpoints but the display does not specify full regularity or time-equality conventions. Nonnegative integration retains infinite action, while Bochner integration requires integrability and must not assign default zero to invalid paths. The later four-times-Hellinger-squared closed form is recorded separately and may not coincide with the intrinsic probability-preserving action; do not substitute it or claim equality from generic integrals.

rows.result: The pure reaction equation can be stated through scalar derivatives of smooth compactly supported test-function integrals.
rows.gap: The distributional evolution and its analytic admissibility remain to be constructed with the exact first-variation representative; the library ingredients do not prove flow existence.

comparisons.D12: For each smooth compactly supported test phi require d/dt integral phi drho_t = -integral phi*(1+delta_ell_N(rho_t)) drho_t, with no transport/divergence term. This is the source distributional reading and applies to atomic measures as well as densities; a pointwise PDE for a Lebesgue density would restrict the domain. The explicit first variation has rho_t-mean -1, making the reaction centered. A first variation defined only modulo constants cannot be substituted without adjusting that 1 term. HasDerivAt gives scalar derivative notation but does not select an almost-everywhere time or right-derivative convention, supply necessary integrability, prove probability preservation or construct a unique curve. The source refers to an excluded appendix for the geometry derivation; no such proof is imported into the census.
